person_made_it: A person sat with the actual episode for an hour tonight and found that its first nineteen minutes are the class's own annotation exercise performed by the cast, then drew the doorway scene as a floor plan; no template produces either of those.
emcee_who_is_speaking: One voice, talking to Gordon alone at a podium at 10:00 AM, in the imperative and in his own vocabulary, and it says out loud which things are mine and which are lifted from his Teacher's Guide.
what_time_of_day_is_this_room: Monday morning, fluorescent, SCI L104, 170 minutes with a room that has not had coffee; the palette is paper-white and one burnt cardinal, which is a lecture hall at 10 AM and not an evening keynote.
did_the_click_pay_me: Yes: it opens on the two things that can wreck the morning (a Zoom that ends when class starts, and a 30-minute play call pointed at an 86-second clip) before it asks for anything.
works_for_the_recipient: It prints to seven letter pages, survives JavaScript being off, and now holds at 390px because he opens links on his phone; the run sheet is wall-clock so he never has to do arithmetic mid-sentence.
taught_me_something: That an oEmbed 200 proves a video exists and nothing else, and that a caption track is a free, exact, primary source for what happens inside a video when chapters do not exist.
told_me_the_truth: Yes, including against myself: the Gordon/Alex clash I printed this evening was a stale recurring hold, it is marked NOT TODAY with the reason, and the footer says plainly that captions timestamp speech but cannot tell you what the camera did.
weakest: Diagram B argues the cut takes your choice away without showing a single real frame from the Hamilton edit, so it is a diagram of an idea rather than of that tape; if I had a signed-in browser I would replace the right panel with three actual stills at 0:29, 0:33 and 0:37.
